biodiversity_overview.text: 5,866 GBIF occurrence records for 11 tracked species are attributed to Ladakh, spanning 1876-2026.
5,803 of these records (98.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 7, Mammalia 2, Magnoliopsida 2.

threatened_species.text: 2 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Mountain Chiffchaff (5,538), Indian Golden Oriole (216), Indian peninsular wolf (56), Indian Pond-heron (28), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (19).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 157 in 2016 to 16 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 22.45% of Ladakh's area (4 areas intersect the state).
23.2% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (1,348 of 5,803); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Belladonna (0.30), Common Leopard (0.25), Mountain Chiffchaff (0.20), Indian Trumpet Tree (0.13), Indian peninsular wolf (0.10).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Ladakh (equal-weight reference): cell near 34.125N 76.125E (overall rank 402, median rank across weightings 394); cell near 35.625N 76.875E (overall rank 468, median rank across weightings 462); cell near 33.375N 76.875E (overall rank 499, median rank across weightings 499).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 632 km2 (0.36% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

1.3 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.2% of the 2000 extent; 0.02% in 2015-2024, rank 31 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2003 (0.21 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.02% of land and population density is 7.9 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
69% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
